messages:
Ari Summers: RFC follow-up: propose 'edge-guard mesh' where routers make fast local fallback decisions using a signed policy snapshot + short leases. central plane only for policy and auditing. quick reactions, audited central override. thoughts?
Ben Cho: signed snapshot + lease is good. how do we avoid inconsistent cuts across routers?
Ari Summers: leases short (8-12s). routers broadcast local verdicts to telemetry; control plane reconciles and can revoke by bumping epoch with enforce=true.
Priya Raman: need per-tenant min_live_pct so a single router can't zero a tenant. also tenant risk_budget for progressive cuts.
Marco Diaz: cache churn concern when routing flips to older variant. suggest 'warm-shadow': small fraction of traffic mirrored to fallback to keep caches warm during cut.
Ben Cho: add hysteresis: cooldown_ms and backoff_factor for rejoin attempts. include recovery_confidence_window_s before full rejoin.
Ari Summers: decision provenance required. attach decision_id and verdict_reason (probe/error/override) to request traces and metrics.
ops-bot: reminder: warm-shadow increases downstream QPS and may trigger rate-limits; document in runbook.
Priya Raman: control plane should include 'grace_window_s' for non-force overrides so in-flight requests finish. force flag bypasses grace.
Marco Diaz: what about network partition? if control plane unreachable, routers honor last valid signed snapshot until lease expiry then default to divert-to-fallback safe-mode.
Ari Summers: thanks, I'll update the snapshot schema (epoch, lease_ttl_s, rules, tenant_overrides, force) and open a short PR for telemetry hooks and runbook mapping.
Ben Cho: +1. schedule a 20m sync with eng-sre to map alerts to sentinel states.
Priya Raman: ack, will draft tenant override examples.
